definitions.explanation: So painful, difficult, or unpleasant that it is extremely hard to bear or put up with.

examples.japanese: {耐|た}え{難|がた}い⟦{痛|いた}み→痛み：01795_itami⟧だ。
{耐|た}え{難|がた}い⟦{暑|あつ}さ→暑さ：12973_atsusa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧、⟦{作業|さぎょう}→作業：02775_sagyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧た。
examples.english: They continued working in the unbearable heat.

examples.japanese: ⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧、⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧。
examples.english: Enduring the unendurable, bearing the unbearable.
examples.notes: Famous phrase from Emperor Showa's 1945 radio address announcing Japan's surrender.

notes:
Formed from ⟦{耐|た}える→耐える：12087_taeru⟧ (to endure) + ⟦{難|がた}い→難い：17198_gatai⟧ (difficult to ~). A literary and formal expression for extreme difficulty in enduring something. Also written ⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧がたい, with the がたい part in kana; both spellings are common.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase ⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧、⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧ is one of the most famous lines in modern Japanese history, from the {玉音放送|ぎょくおんほうそう} (Imperial radio broadcast) on August 15, 1945, in which Emperor Showa announced Japan's surrender.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い⟦{痛|いた}み→痛み：01795_itami⟧ — unbearable pain
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い⟦{苦|くる}しみ→苦しみ：14120_kurushimi⟧ — intolerable suffering
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い⟦{屈辱|くつじょく}→屈辱：04853_kutsujoku⟧ — unbearable humiliation
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い⟦{暑|あつ}さ→暑さ：12973_atsusa⟧ — unbearable heat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{我慢|がまん}できない→我慢する：25343_gamansuru⟧ — can't stand it; more colloquial
- ⟦{信|しん}じ{難|がた}い→信じ難い：19679_shinjigatai⟧ — hard to believe; same ～⟦{難|がた}い→難い：17198_gatai⟧ pattern
- {堪|た}えられない — unbearable; spoken/colloquial equivalent
